name: Domaine Grand Veneur Châteauneuf-du-Pape Les Origines 2010
text:
## Domaine Grand Veneur Châteauneuf-du-Pape Les Origines 2010

**The story.** [Domaine Grand Veneur](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+Grand+Veneur,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k) belongs to the Jaume family, who first planted vines in [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC) in 1826, under Mathieu Jaume. Five generations later, in 1979, Alain and Odile Jaume took over what was then a traditional estate of just 4.5 hectares. Alain changed it fast. In 1986 Grand Veneur became perhaps the first estate in Châteauneuf to age some of its wine in new French [oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_%28wine%29) barrels, and the family kept buying land until the domaine reached its present size ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). His children Sébastien, Christophe and Hélène now run it with him ([Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2017-domaine-grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-vieilles-vignes_71ace8f7-b8e3-4437-bdba-1d509301d42a/)). Alain's brother Patrick owns a neighbouring estate, [Domaine des Chanssaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=Domaine+des+Chanssaud&go=Go).

Today the family has 16 hectares in Châteauneuf, plus vines across the river in [Lirac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC) ([see it from above](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Lirac,+Gard,+France&t=k)), where they bought the 9-hectare Clos de Sixte in 2003, and in the [Côtes du Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%B4tes_du_Rh%C3%B4ne_AOC). Lirac sits on the right bank of the [Rhône](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rh%C3%B4ne), next to the rosé-only appellation of [Tavel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tavel_AOC) ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lirac_AOC)). Jeff Leve of The Wine Cellar Insider calls Grand Veneur one of his favourite Châteauneuf producers, and says it still offers a lot of value and character for the money. The Wine Advocate has called it "one of the most brilliant estates in Châteauneuf-du-Pape" (quoted by [Wine Access](https://www.wineaccess.com/catalog/2017-domaine-grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-vieilles-vignes_71ace8f7-b8e3-4437-bdba-1d509301d42a/)).

**The wine: Les Origines.** "The origins" is Grand Veneur's other prestige red, a step below the Vieilles Vignes and made in much larger quantity, about 1,400 cases a year. It is an unusual blend for Châteauneuf, with only about half [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) and the rest split between [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) and [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre), from vines more than 65 years old. It is modern in style, aged for about 16 months in a mix of new and used French [oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_%28wine%29) barrels ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)). Jeff Leve calls it "another contender in the high quality, fair price sweepstakes".

For 2010, Robert Parker gives the blend as 50% Grenache, 30% Syrah and 20% Mourvèdre from vines 45 to 95 years old, aged in small oak; Jeb Dunnuck, then writing The Rhône Report, says 18 months in new oak ([JJ Buckley, critics' notes](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2010-domaine-grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-cuvee-les-origines/2010-7333-1500)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) calls 2010 a very successful southern Rhône vintage, with precision and freshness letting the terroir show, outstanding for reds and whites, though she adds that the wines perhaps haven't matured quite as spectacularly as first expected. The same vintage brought the estate a perfect 100-point score from Parker for its Vieilles Vignes ([Farr Vintners](https://www.farrvintners.com/wine.php?wine=33868)).

**What the critics say for 2010.** As listed by [JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2010-domaine-grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-cuvee-les-origines/2010-7333-1500):
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck), The Rhône Report: 98** (March 2012). More edgy and precise than the 2007: black cherry, blackberry liqueur, graphite, licorice, spice box and roasted meats; full-bodied, structured and concentrated, with excellent freshness, brilliant purity and a mineral-laced finish. Not for "instant gratification": give it 4 to 5 years, then drink over the following 15 to 20.
- **[Robert Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Parker_%28wine_critic%29), Wine Advocate: 95** (October 2012). "Another blockbuster": opaque purple, with blackberries, espresso roast, ink and graphite. Clearly modern, but it "retains plenty of the region's typicity and authenticity". Should drink well for 15-plus years.
- **[Wine Spectator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Spectator): 92** (James Molesworth, July 2012). Racy, with dark bramble, [linzer torte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linzertorte) and blackberry, and a strong graphite edge; it gains density on the finish. Best 2014 to 2022.
- **Jeff Leve, [The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/): 93**. Ripe black cherries, black raspberries, smoke, vanilla and herbs; "round, fat, lush, fresh and delicious".
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.2** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is sixteen years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2018 to 2027; Wine Spectator's ran only to 2022, while Parker's 15-plus years and Dunnuck's 4 to 5 years plus 15 to 20 take it to about 2027 to 2036. So it is mature: open it in the next year or two. The new oak should be fully absorbed by now, leaving graphite, licorice, dried black fruit and savoury notes. Decant gently.

**Serving.** The Wine Cellar Insider suggests serving Grand Veneur at about 15.5°C, almost cellar temperature, for freshness and lift. Younger bottles benefit from 1 to 2 hours in a [decanter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decantation); older ones need only enough to leave the sediment behind. It says Grand Veneur is usually best with 4 to 6 years in bottle, and the best vintages drink well from 5 to 20 years after the harvest ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).

**Food.** The Wine Cellar Insider suggests classic meat dishes (veal, pork, beef, lamb, duck, game, roast chicken, braises, sausages, barbecue and [cassoulet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cassoulet)), as well as mushrooms, eggplant and cheese. My picks: a [rack of lamb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rack_of_lamb) with garlic and rosemary, a Provençal beef [daube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daube), a mushroom [pappardelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pappardelle), or [venison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venison) with a pepper sauce. I'd avoid delicate fish and very spicy food.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the three stores on this site lists Les Origines at the moment. Back vintages turn up with merchants such as [JJ Buckley](https://www.jjbuckley.com/wine/2010-domaine-grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-cuvee-les-origines/2010-7333-1500) and at auction. It has long been one of the fairer-priced prestige Châteauneufs.

**From the history books**
- **The popes and their castle.** In 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V) moved the papacy to [Avignon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Palais+des+Papes,+Avignon,+France&t=k), beginning the [Avignon Papacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon_Papacy). His successor [John XXII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_XXII) improved the vineyards to the north and built the summer [castle](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Ch%C3%A2teau+des+Papes,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k) that gave the village its name, "the Pope's new castle" ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **1826, the first Jaume vines.** The Jaume family planted its first vines in Châteauneuf in 1826, a generation before the [phylloxera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_French_Wine_Blight) louse devastated French vineyards in the 1870s ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/); [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **France's first appellation.** Fraud was so common in the early 20th century that local growers, led by Baron [Pierre Le Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Le_Roy_de_Boiseaumari%C3%A9) of [Château Fortia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Fortia), drew up rules in 1923 that became France's first [appellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e) rules, made law in 1936 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **Small barrels, 1986.** Châteauneuf has traditionally aged its wine in large old casks and concrete, partly because Grenache oxidises easily in small barrels ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)). Alain Jaume's experiments with new [oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_%28wine%29) barrels in 1986 put Grand Veneur among the pioneers of a more modern style.

**Curious details**
- **The royal huntsman.** "Grand Veneur" is French for the Grand Huntsman, once one of the great offices of the French royal household, the master of the king's hunt ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Huntsman_of_France)).
- **A white near Beaucastel.** The estate's rare white, La Fontaine, is 100% old-vine [Roussanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roussanne) from a single parcel not far from [Château de Beaucastel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_de_Beaucastel), with only about 200 cases made ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).
- **A cuvée with a geological name.** Another Grand Veneur wine, La Miocène, first made in the difficult 2013 vintage, shares its name with the [Miocene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miocene), the geological age of 23 to 5 million years ago ([The Wine Cellar Insider](https://www.thewinecellarinsider.com/rhone-wines-cote-rotie-hermitage-chateauneuf-du-pape/chateauneuf-du-pape-wine-producer-profiles/grand-veneur-chateauneuf-du-pape-rhone-wine/)).
- **Two brothers, two estates.** Like the Usseglios, the Jaume brothers each run their own domaine: Alain at Grand Veneur, Patrick at Domaine des Chanssaud.
- **Why the blend matters.** In Châteauneuf, [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache) gives sweet, ripe, almost jam-like juice when very ripe; [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) adds colour and spice; and [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre) brings elegance and structure. Wines with a lot of Mourvèdre tend to be more tannic and need longer in the cellar. Grenache covered about 72% of the appellation's vineyards in 2004, Mourvèdre only about 7% ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **The flying-cigar law.** In 1954, after local reports of [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_saucer), the Châteauneuf council banned "flying cigars" from flying over or landing in the commune. The decree is still in force, and a Californian Rhône-style wine from [Bonny Doon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonny_Doon_Vineyard), Le Cigare Volant, is named after the tale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
